paper.title_en: Vestiges of magnon fractionalization in the quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet rouaite Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ with alternating ferro- and antiferromagnetic $S=\frac{1}{2}$ chains
paper.abstract_en: Ferro- and antiferromagnetic quantum spin chains host qualitatively distinct elementary excitations --- magnons ($S=1$, bosonic quasiparticles) and spinons ($S=\frac{1}{2}$, fractionalized quasiparticles), respectively. Weakly coupled networks of both chain types therefore provide an ideal platform for exploring spinon-magnon coupling and the hybridization of sharp magnon modes with spinon continua. Here we investigate the spin-excitation spectrum of the frustrated quantum magnet rouaite, Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ --- a model realization of weakly coupled ferro- and antiferromagnetic Cu$^{2+}$ spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ chains. The frustrated interchain interactions, while weaker than the dominant intrachain exchange, are sufficient to stabilize a long-range-ordered state that is not reproduced by classical calculations. Neutron spectroscopy reveals a spectrum of well-defined spin waves associated with both types of chains, with clear signatures of hybridization but no observable spinon continuum. Certain magnon branches resulting from this hybridization exhibit substantial broadening near the zone center. We attribute this to vestiges of spinon fractionalization persisting partway through the dimensional crossover from isolated quantum spin chains to a 2D network of frustrated spins.
